title: Section principal cone maps to quotient tensors
statement:
Fix a prime l, a finite extension E/Q_l and a scheme X. Use the strict section scalar presentation and actual section quotient objects [def-sfb-strict-completion-restriction-data]. For each K-flat complex P there are quasi-isomorphisms from its strict principal-cone levels to P tensor B_n whose degree q maps are the first-projection coordinate followed by x maps to x tensor 1. This statement asserts only the individual level maps and their fixed coordinate formula, not successor compatibility, the augmented product map or completion. Precisely:

theorem strictSectionQuotientConeMaps (X : Scheme.{u})
    (T : Presentation.{u + 2, u + 1, u + 1}
      (Modules (DerivedNakayama.integerRing l E) X))
    (data : PrincipalReduction.PrincipalReductionConeData l E X)
    (hdata : data.IsCanonical l E X)
    (hscalar : ∀ (M : Modules (DerivedNakayama.integerRing l E) X) (U : X.ProEtᵒᵖ)
      (x : M.val.obj U),
      (T.scalar.app M).val.app U x = sectionScalarValue l E X data.d U • x)
    (B : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) CommRingCat.{u + 1})
    (ι : (Functor.const ℕᵒᵖ).obj (ring (DerivedNakayama.integerRing l E) X) ⟶ B)
    (hB : ∀ n : ℕ, B.obj (op n) = sectionRingSheaf.{u + 1, u + 1, u} (Scheme.ProEt.topology X)
        (AdicCompletion.finiteRing l E X n))
    (hι : ∀ n : ℕ, HEq (ι.app (op n))
        (sectionScalarMap.{u + 1, u + 1, u} (Scheme.ProEt.topology X)
          (AdicCompletion.quotient l E X n)))
    (P : CochainComplex (Modules (DerivedNakayama.integerRing l E) X) ℤ)
    (hP : CochainComplex.IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients
      (R := ring (DerivedNakayama.integerRing l E) X) P) :
    ∃ c : ∀ n : ℕ, (T.tower.obj P).asFunctor.obj (op n) ⟶
        (SheafOfModules.KFlatRoos.level.{u + 1, u, u + 1} B ι n).obj P,
      (∀ n : ℕ, QuasiIso (c n)) ∧
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (q : ℤ), (c n).f q =
        (T.coordinates P n q).hom ≫ biprod.fst ≫
          (SheafOfModules.KFlatRoos.tensorUnit.{u + 1, u, u + 1}
            (ι.app (op n))).app (P.X q))

source.place: Locality; first-reduction Cones paragraph and Stacks tags in the Lean docstring. Normalized principal quotient tensor models and augmented section completion

proof.text: Identify the section image of each finite internal coefficient module with the specified algebra module by finiteModuleIso, sectionModuleComapIso and sectionModuleRegularIso. Sheafify the section tensor comparison and this coefficient isomorphism. Naturality of sheafification gives its pure-tensor formula; the internal right unitor and finiteUnit send x to x tensor 1, so it agrees with the prescribed tensorUnit. Assemble degreewise into an isomorphism of complexes.

Take the inverse image K of P under the termwise section equivalence. The counit and total-tensor comparison transfer K-flatness to K. Equality on local sections identifies the internal scalar action with T.scalar, and scalarOnModules_pow identifies their positive powers. Apply the already proved internal coneToTensor_quasiIso to K. The mapHomologicalComplexIso_hom_descShortComplex identity and the naturality of cone descent transport its quasi-isomorphism through the exact section equivalence, the counit and the tensor comparison. The cone map induced by the counit is an actual isomorphism: map the inverse square and use mappingCone.map_comp and mappingCone.map_id. The transport proof is checked over an abstract coefficient ring before the canonical scalar data are supplied.

Transport the cone augmentation across T.cone. Its degree component is the unshifted cone projection followed by tensorUnit, and T.coordinates_eq gives the stated biproduct formula. Eliminate the supplied quotient-object equality and heterogeneous coefficient-map equality at each n, then choose the resulting family. Empty sites and zero quotients use the same identities; no nonzero section or lifting of quotient sections is assumed.

proof_origin: G2: transport of the proved internal coefficient-cone augmentation, with direct sheafification comparison and normalized local pure tensors; no new obligations.
